title: Who Can Evaluate AI Independently? A Framework for Analysing Evaluation Infrastructure
abstract: arXiv:2611.08134v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI evaluation is increasingly central to AI safety and governance, yet taking part in an evaluation does not by itself confer authority over its design, its execution or the resources it depends on. This paper examines how infrastructure arrangements distribute that authority, and so shape who can evaluate AI systems independently. Drawing on Science and Technology Studies, political economy and applied evaluation standards, we introduce PAAI (Power, Access, Adequacy, Independence), a framework for examining who controls evaluation infrastructure, the terms on which it is available, whether it is adequate to the evaluation's purpose and what autonomy it supports. We apply PAAI to twelve African AI evaluation projects (2022-2025) and to the documented roles of all ten member institutes in the three published joint testing exercises of the international network of AI Safety Institutes. translated_title: 谁能独立评估人工智能？一个用于分析评估基础设施的框架
translated_abstract: 人工智能评估在AI安全与治理中日益处于核心地位，然而参与评估本身并不意味着对评估的设计、执行或其所依赖的资源拥有权威。本文研究了基础设施安排如何分配这种权威，从而决定谁能够独立地评估人工智能系统。借鉴科学技术研究（STS）、政治经济学和应用评估标准，我们提出了PAAI（权力、可及性、充分性、独立性）框架，用于考察谁控制评估基础设施、基础设施可用的条件、它是否足以满足评估目的，以及它支持何种自主性。我们将PAAI应用于十二个非洲人工智能评估项目（2022-2025年），以及人工智能安全研究所国际网络三次已发布联合测试活动中全部十个成员研究所的公开角色。我们识别出三种反复出现的配置模式：抽取式……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出PAAI（权力、可及性、充分性、独立性）分析框架，通过考察评估基础设施的权威分配，结合非洲AI评估项目与国际AI安全研究所网络的案例，揭示谁能够真正独立地评估AI系统。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the PAAI (Power, Access, Adequacy, Independence) framework for analyzing how evaluation infrastructure distributes authority, applying it to African AI evaluation projects and the AI Safety Institutes network to determine who can independently evaluate AI systems.
